title: One Man Planted a Forest Bigger Than Central Park
yt_title: One Man Planted a Forest Bigger Than Central Park 🌳 #shorts
yt_description:
In 1979, a young man in Assam, India found snakes dead on a bare sandbar of the Brahmaputra River – there was no shade. Jadav "Molai" Payeng started planting bamboo, then trees. Year after year, the sand turned into a 550-hectare forest – home to rhinos, tigers and a herd of around 100 elephants.

Forest officials only found out in 2008. Today he's known as the Forest Man of India, and the forest carries his nickname: Molai.

A true story. Sources: Mongabay, Wikipedia, Times of India.

#unsungstories #forestman #truestory #nature #inspiration #shorts
script: In nineteen seventy-nine, a young man in India found dozens of snakes lying dead on a sandbar in the Brahmaputra River. There wasn't a single tree to give them shade. His name was Jadav Payeng. And he decided to fix it. He moved onto the empty sand... and started planting bamboo. Other workers planted there too. Then they left. Jadav stayed. One tree. A hundred. Thousands. Year after year, the sand turned green. Then the animals came back. Rhinos. Tigers. And every year, a herd of about a hundred elephants. For almost thirty years, the forest department had no idea. Then, in two thousand eight, officers finally reached the island... and were stunned to find a thick, wild forest. Five hundred and fifty hectares. Bigger than New York's Central Park. Planted by one man. Today, people call him the Forest Man of India. And the forest carries his nickname... Molai.
